chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi'i ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is proper for the scholar, when asked about something he does not know, to say: God knows best. And it is not proper for one who is not a scholar to say that.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ: God knows best; an expression of epistemic humility, a formula permitted specifically for scholars when they lack knowledge of a matter
key_terms.الْعَالِم: The scholar; one who possesses religious knowledge ('ilm), particularly jurisprudential and theological knowledge
key_terms.لِغَيْرِ الْعَالِمِ: For other than the scholar; those who do not possess the requisite qualification of religious learning

ai.seo_question: Can anyone say 'Allah knows best' when asked about a religious matter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes an important distinction regarding the phrase 'Allah knows best' (Allahu a'lam). This teaching addresses the problem of unqualified persons issuing religious opinions — such a person cannot claim epistemic humility through that formula, as that phrase itself implies a recognized scholarly standing. The hadith thus simultaneously promotes intellectual honesty in scholars and guards against the appropriation of scholarly authority by the unqualified.
